results.notes: Source: saved NBER manuscript, PDF pp. 12-13, Figure 1B/1D; Table 1, PDF pp. 18-19. The validated grade variable is overall, an evaluator's 1-7 overall-quality rating, not an arithmetic composite of writing, content, and originality. Treatment is randomized ChatGPT access (treatment=1), control is Overleaf signup (treatment=0); actual ChatGPT use does not determine inclusion. Reconstruction follows osf-xd7qw/code/2 - clean.do, 3 - grade cleaning_jul21.do, and 4 - main text figures.do, read only as text. The July 21 grade-cleaning version removes the original script's unavailable private anonymization-file merge; all other grade-cleaning steps are identical. Survey exclusions: unfinished/nonconsenting responses; later duplicate submissions; six explicitly listed manual exclusions; qcheck outside 1 after recoding 3 to 1; and people who had graded before doing the task survey. These steps leave 453 people (218 treatment, 235 control), matching the printed descriptive sample. The linear/convex restriction leaves 359 (172 treatment, 187 control). Long-form ratings exclude the named test grader, retry=1 edited/resubmitted first-task outputs, graders who graded after participating in the task survey, missing overall scores, and 23 of 118 assessed graders whose own-vs-other grade regression slope is below 0.1. Every possible orientation of tied same-grader pairs gives the same exclusion decisions. Post-treatment means essay B when a_first=1 and essay A when a_first=0. The Figure 1D reconstruction contains 462 treatment and 501 control ratings from 167 treatment and 186 control people. The paper does not print these Figure 1 analysis counts: reproduced count checks above concern the full descriptive/baseline samples, not inferred printed post-treatment Ns. For computed statistics each person's retained post-treatment overall ratings are averaged first; people then receive equal weight. SDs use n-1. The participant means consequently differ from the paper's rating-weighted means. difference is treatment_mean minus control_mean in 1-7 grade points. difference_se is OLS with an intercept and arm indicator, HC2, at the individually randomized participant level; it is also independently checked as sqrt(treatment_sd^2/n_treatment + control_sd^2/n_control). Separately, Figure 1B is reproduced from 1000 participant-evaluator rows and 352 people (166 treatment, 186 control) with both grades: raw adjusted coefficient 0.698067260482, participant-clustered SE 0.153804202732, divided by baseline rating SD 1.70404045662. This uses grader, occupation-by-task-order, and incentive fixed effects, and the authors' rounding sequence for the displayed CI. That adjusted change coefficient and clustered SE are validation quantities, not the unadjusted participant difference and HC2 SE requested here. The long- and wide-format analysis populations are intentionally distinguished. This is a between-person RCT with a pre-intervention baseline, not randomized condition order, so round is all and no first_round contrast is produced. The other supplied deposit, osf-q3gdu, was inventoried (769 survey rows, 3774 long rating rows, 1882 wide rows); it is a different dataset and is not pooled with osf-xd7qw. SHA256 checks against the supplied manifest pass for all consulted deposited files. data_files lists data and contextual sources actually read.

skipped.reason: PDF p. 4 prints 0.45 SD (p<0.001), but does not identify a separate sample, standardizer, model, or analysis count. The documented main grade-change specification recomputes to 0.409654159189 SD, or 0.41 at printed precision, matching Figure 1B rather than the narrative's 0.45. Its p-value is 7.78730857413e-06, satisfying the prose bound but not reproducing the effect size. No independent statistics are computed for this unreproduced narrative record, and the Figure 1 result is not duplicated or assigned to it.

The posted grading data contain the originality variable, but this separate extraction record has no printed arm means, difference/coefficient, uncertainty, or outcome-specific counts. PDF p. 4 says only that increases were similar. Supplementary grade results are not embedded in the saved 19-page PDF. An estimate-specific numerical reproduction check is therefore unavailable; no participant statistics are computed under the reproduce-first rule.
